body:
I think there's value in trying to ensure a consistent ShadowRealm environment where you know it always has the same capabilities; of course you still have to feature test as features get added so that reasoning is a bit weak. But the idea is that if ShadowRealm doesn't have a capability that you want, but the surrounding realm has, then you pass it in via the callable boundary.

That said, I'm not super attached to it. If no one else is either, fine with me to leave it as is.

I might very well be misunderstanding how this works (apologies if that's the case!), but I am struggling to see how the "current realm" or "current principal realm" here differs from the "underlying realm".

From what I understand, https://github.com/tc39/proposal-shadowrealm/pull/392 will call `InitializeShadowRealm()` via [InitializeHostDefinedRealm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-initializehostdefinedrealm), with the steps:

> 11. Push newContext onto the [execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack); newContext is now the [running execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).
> 12. If the [host](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#host) requires use of an [exotic object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#exotic-object) to serve as realm's [global object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-global-object), then
    a. Let global be such an object created in a [host-defined](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#host-defined) manner.

In `InitializeShadowRealm()`, `HostInitializeShadowRealm` is then invoked using the current Javascript execution context's realm and that context itself - which should be the newly created `newContext`.

> 1. Let context be the running Javascript execution context.
> 2. Let realm be the Realm of context.
> 3. Return ? HostInitializeShadowRealm(realm, context).

As I understand, this means that when we hit: `HostInitializeShadowRealm` here `realm` which is passed in as an argument is also the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm). But if they are the same thing, how does [current principal realm](https://whatpr.org/html/9893/webappapis.html#current-principal-realm) work given we have not performed:

> Set realm.[[HostDefined]] to settings.

By that stage for that realm?

If I'm understanding this correctly, here the _current principal realm_ and the _current realm_ always correspond, because the DOM is not exposed in shadow realms.

However, I'd prefer if every time we create a new object / function we did it using the _current realm_. Where there is a difference between the two we always want to use the _current realm_, because we don't want to accidentally expose objects from different realms, and where there is no difference... well, they are the same.

Always using the _current realm_ avoids problems when somebody writes a new algorithm looking at an existing one: maybe in the one they are looking at the distinction doesn't matter, so it uses _current principal realm_, and they end up using the _current principal realm_ in a case where actually they need the _current realm_.

The same applies to the functions created in CrossOriginGetOwnPropertyHelper.

**EDIT:** To clarify, I'm _not_ saying that _current Realm_ should transparently return the _current principal Realm_. I'm saying that the _current principal Realm_ concept is not needed at all because where the distinction matters you actually want the non-principal one.

Some more information here as to why I think there may be an issue here. As I understand it, `referrer` for `evaluate` should basically be the result of: [GetActiveScriptOrModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getactivescriptormodule) which importantly has this requirement:

> whose ScriptOrModule component is not null

The ShadowRealm spec will set `ScriptOrModule` to `null` in [PrepareForWrappedFunctionCall](https://tc39.es/proposal-shadowrealm/#sec-prepare-for-wrapped-function-call)

> 6. Set the ScriptOrModule of calleeContext to null.
> 7. If callerContext is not already suspended, suspend callerContext.
> 8. Push calleeContext onto the [execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack); calleeContext is now the [running execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).

Whereas [PrepareForOrdinaryCall](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-prepareforordinarycall) or [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation) does set it to something non-null.

This is not an issue for `importValue` as [ShadowRealmImportValue](https://tc39.es/proposal-shadowrealm/#sec-shadowrealmimportvalue) directly invokes `HostLoadImportedModule` passing through a ShadowRealm, whereas `evaluate` relies on the execution context stack, where nowhere appears to be setting `ScriptOrModule` for the shadow realm case, resulting in module loading going up the execution context stack to find the the script invoking "evaluate" as the referrer (coming from , instead of the shadow realm itself.
